name: Geopost Vision
short: Street-level imagery of Europe from delivery-van dashcams; contact the provider.
summary: Geopost Vision SAS (France), a Geopost venture, sells street-level imagery and telemetry captured by connected dashcams fitted to selected DPD, Chronopost, SEUR and BRT delivery vehicles across Europe. The provider's use-cases page says data is available through an API; no API documentation, price or licence terms are published, and the only route in is a contact form.

tasks: road sign, speed limit and traffic light change detection (object-level insights, per press release)
map updates and road network validation
training and validation imagery for ADAS and autonomous driving
road surface and signage condition monitoring
infrastructure inventory for smart cities and insurance

pricing.notes: Not published. No page read states a price or a pricing model.

latency.typical: Not published; the provider says data collection never stops
latency.notes: The solution page says 'data collection never stops' (vendor claim) with no refresh interval. A January 2026 trade article says data is 'often refreshed on an hourly basis' (secondary, not on the provider's own site). The home-page coverage counters render as placeholders (0), so no real figure is given.

regions: Europe (21 countries listed as live on the provider's solution page; vendor claim)
coverage.notes: The solution page (read 2026-11-04) lists 21 countries as live: UK, France, Spain, Italy, Germany, Hungary, Slovakia, Ireland, Czech Republic, Portugal, Netherlands, Poland, Belgium, Bulgaria, Romania, Latvia, Estonia, Luxembourg, Croatia, Slovenia, Lithuania. The 3 Dec 2025 Geopost press release said 11 live and 10 planned for mid-2026, and a 14 Jan 2026 trade article repeated 11 with more than 20 targeted by end 2026, so the 21-country list is the provider's later self-report. Density within a country is not published; the vans are a delivery fleet, so rural and off-route roads may be sparse.

licensing.summary: No licence, usage-rights, AI-training or resale terms are published. The legal notice covers only the website's content (reuse requires prior consent) and the use-cases and solution pages state no data licence. Rights would be set in a contract after contact. The privacy page says the footage is recorded and processed jointly with Geopost.

human.unknown: Capture is passive by delivery drivers' vehicles. No enrolment or identity check of a person is described, and none is needed for the claim; the capturing people are not identified.

application.unknown: No app or device attestation is documented. A trade article describes the camera as a Nextbase IQ connected dashcam.

camera.unknown: No signed capture is documented, and neither Geopost nor Nextbase is on the C2PA conforming products list (checked 2026-11-04). The provider says the cameras are connected dashcams on its own fleet vehicles.

time.method: Telemetry is logged alongside imagery, including timestamps
time.unknown: Whether timestamps are from a trusted source or signed, and whether the time is delivered with each image, is not documented.

location.method: GPS coordinates (longitude, latitude, altitude), HDOP, VDOP, PDOP, heading, speed and IMU are logged with the imagery
location.unknown: Position is device-reported GNSS with quality metrics; spoofing resistance and signing are not documented.

content.method: Provider states the imagery is delivered 'fully anonymized and GDPR-compliant' (vendor claim)
content.unknown: No integrity check (hash, signature) is documented. The press release (not the provider's own pages) says faces and licence plates are removed.

corroboration.unknown: No independent cross-check is documented. Repeat passes by several vans may overlap, but the provider does not say that is used for confirmation.

auth.how_to_get: Contact form at https://www.geopost-vision.com/en/contact/ or contact@geopost-vision.com; no key issuance process is published.

api.notes: The use-cases page says 'Through our API, teams can also improve routing accuracy'; the press release says data is delivered 'through APIs to clients including mapping providers'. No documentation, base URL, endpoints, formats or OpenAPI file was found. No /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource or oauth-authorization-server on the provider's domain (404, 2026-11-04). Not in the official MCP Registry (searched 'geopost', 2026-11-04).

mcp.notes: No MCP server found; the official registry search for 'geopost' returned none.

delivery.basis: No turnaround or delivery mode is published; the provider says only that data collection never stops.

requester.unknown: No check of who requests data, or for what purpose, is published; the contact form asks first and last name, email, optional work phone, company and a message.

sources.claim: Article dated 14 Jan 2026: Geopost Vision CEO Martin Calmels; Nextbase IQ connected dashcam, 4K imagery at 30 FPS, GPS up to 10 Hz; customers retrieve imagery through an API; 11 countries, goal of 20+ by end 2026; data often refreshed hourly; four verticals (mapping, mobility, insurance, road maintenance)
Cameras on selected DPD, Chronopost, SEUR and BRT vehicles; imagery 'fully anonymized and GDPR-compliant'; counters render as 0; no API or price mentioned

Telemetry (timestamps, lat/long/altitude, HDOP/VDOP/PDOP, heading, speed, IMU); up to 4K, 30 FPS, 140 degree view; 21 countries listed live; 'data collection never stops'; no API, anonymisation, licence or price stated
Use cases (mapping and navigation, autonomous driving and ADAS, smart cities, road maintenance, insurance); mentions 'our API'; no licence, price or refresh interval
Legal notice: Geopost Vision SAS, 26 rue Guynemer, Issy-les-Moulineaux, RCS Nanterre 878 301 407; website content needs prior consent to reuse; no clause on data, AI or automated access
Privacy page: Geopost Vision records video of the road and street environment via connected dashcams and jointly processes it with Geopost; anonymisation and retention not stated on this page

Press release 3 Dec 2025: 11 live and 10 planned countries; strict anonymization removing faces and licence plates; imagery never made publicly available; data delivered through APIs to clients including mapping providers
Post&Parcel: 11 live and 10 planned countries; no raw imagery made publicly available; no pricing mentioned
No Geopost server in the official MCP Registry
Neither Geopost nor Nextbase on the C2PA conforming products list
